The diagram below shows a sequence of shapes made up of black and white floor tiles where each shape after the first has two more rows and two more columns than the one before it.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a sequence of square tile patterns. The 1st shape is a single black tile. The 2nd shape is a 3 by 3 checkerboard-style pattern with black tiles in the four corners and the center, totaling 5 black tiles. The 3rd shape is a 5 by 5 alternating checkerboard pattern with black tiles at the corners, totaling 13 black tiles. The diagram then indicates the sequence continues to the 15th shape. Reasoning: Each shape after the first has two more rows and two more columns than the previous one, so the side lengths are 1, 3, 5, ... . Therefore, the nth shape has side length 2n - 1. For the 15th shape, the side length is 2(15) - 1 = 29. Since the pattern is an alternating checkerboard on an odd by odd square and begins and ends with black corners, the number of black tiles is one more than the number of white tiles. Thus the number of black tiles is (29^2 + 1) / 2 = (841 + 1) / 2 = 421.
